w: Launched from Clydebank in 1936, the Queen Mary held the transatlantic Blue Riband on and off until 1952, and once ferried 16,600 troops in a single WWII crossing, a record that still stands. She's now a permanently moored hotel and museum in Long Beach, her art-deco liner glamour intact.
s: A record-holding ocean liner turned hotel
_facts: Built by John Brown & Co, launched 1936
Won the transatlantic speed's Blue Riband, held it to 1952
Carried 16,600 troops on one 1943 WWII voyage, still a record
Now a permanently moored hotel, museum and convention venue

w: Lead ship of the last class of American battleships ever completed, Iowa carried President Roosevelt to the 1943 Tehran Conference with Churchill and Stalin, later shelled Korean coastlines, and survived a 1989 turret explosion that killed 47 sailors before decommissioning in 1990.
s: FDR's battleship, now a museum ship
_facts: Lead ship of the Iowa-class, last US battleships built
Carried FDR across the Atlantic to the 1943 Tehran Conference
1989 turret explosion killed 47 crew
Decommissioned 1990, now preserved as a museum ship

w: A 6-acre non-profit aquarium on Rainbow Harbor, opened in 1998 across the water from the Queen Mary and Shoreline Village. It draws around 1.7 million visitors a year, run by nearly 500 staff and almost 2,000 volunteers, with its own dedicated street, Aquarium Way, named in its honor.
s: Long Beach's harborside aquarium, its own street
_facts: Opened June 20, 1998, on a 6-acre Rainbow Harbor site
1.7 million visitors in 2018
About 485 employees and 1,979 volunteers in 2024
Has its own address: Aquarium Way

w: The only suspension bridge in greater Los Angeles, this 1,500-foot span opened in 1963 to link San Pedro with Terminal Island across the harbor. It was the first welded suspension bridge built in the United States and remains the fourth-longest of its kind in California.
s: The only suspension bridge in greater LA
_facts: Opened 1963, links San Pedro to Terminal Island
First welded suspension bridge built in the US
Only suspension bridge in the Greater LA area
Fourth-longest suspension bridge in California

w: Also called Angels Gate Light, this lighthouse guards the San Pedro Breakwater at the harbor entrance and is one of only a handful in the country that flashes emerald green rather than white, a quirk shared with just two lighthouses on the New England coast. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
s: One of America's rare green-lit lighthouses
_facts: Also known as Angels Gate Light
Stands on the San Pedro Breakwater, Los Angeles Harbor
One of very few US lighthouses emitting emerald green light
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places

w: A business corridor along Anaheim Street lined with Cambodian restaurants, jewelers, clothing stores, donut shops, Khmer temples and service centers. Also called Little Phnom Penh, it anchors the largest concentration of Cambodians anywhere outside Southeast Asia.

w: A Cold War Foxtrot-class attack submarine commissioned in 1971 for the Soviet Pacific Fleet, decommissioned in 1994, then sold to Australian buyers and displayed first in Sydney before being towed to Long Beach in 1998 as Podvodnaya Lodka B-427. Closed to the public and deteriorating since 2015.
